sections.label: Infrastructure Protection Bill security framework
sections.summary: The Infrastructure Protection Bill ensures critical infrastructure and high-footfall and iconic buildings are designed with security in mind.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Infrastructure Protection Bill sets out such a legal framework.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: First, the Bill will ensure that critical infrastructure, as well as buildings with high public footfall and iconic buildings, are designed with security in mind.

sections.label: Security-by-design and protection directives
sections.summary: The Bill requires a security-by-design process before building or renovation and lets authorities issue directives to protect other buildings against terrorist attacks.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Bill will require such infrastructure to undergo a security-by-design process before they are built or renovated.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill will allow the authorities to issue directives and orders to protect other buildings in Singapore against terrorist attacks.

sections.label: Addressing PAPPA gaps
sections.summary: The Bill addresses gaps in the PAPPA and gives owners enhanced powers to address threats and implement heightened surveillance around the facility.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Bill will address gaps in the PAPPA.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It will give the owners of these locations enhanced powers to address threats and implement heightened surveillance in the area surrounding the facility.

sections.label: Security-by-design legal requirement
sections.summary: Security-by-design will be made a legal requirement under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Security-by-design will be made a legal requirement under the Bill.

sections.label: Designating Special Developments and Infrastructures
sections.summary: The Minister will designate critical infrastructures and large or iconic buildings as Special Developments or Special Infrastructures, including all existing and new critical infrastructures.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Minister will designate two groups of buildings as Special Developments or Special Infrastructures: first, critical infrastructures, which are vital to the delivery of essential services, such as water, power and transport; and second, large or iconic buildings, which face a higher level of threat either due to high public footfall, or because of their prominence or symbolic significance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: All critical infrastructures, whether existing or new, will be designated under the Bill.

sections.label: Penalty for offence
sections.summary: The penalty is a fine of up to $200,000 or two years' jail, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The penalty is a fine of up to $200,000 or two years’ jail, or both.

sections.label: Penalties for directive breaches
sections.summary: Directives under clauses 49 to 54 for Special Infrastructures carry a fine up to $100,000 or two years' jail or both, while clause 55 directives for other buildings carry up to $50,000 or two years' jail or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For directives under clauses 49 to 54, which is applicable to Special Infrastructures, this is punishable by a fine of up to $100,000 or imprisonment of up to two years or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For directives under clause 55, which is applicable to buildings not designated as Special Infrastructure, this is punishable by a fine of up to $50,000 or imprisonment of up to two years or both.

sections.label: Minister's imminent terrorist attack orders
sections.summary: Clause 58 empowers the Minister to issue an order to any premises to take immediate actions against an imminent risk of a terrorist attack.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To address any imminent risk of a terrorist attack, clause 58 empowers the Minister to issue an order to any premises to take immediate actions against that risk.

sections.label: Penalty for non-compliance with orders
sections.summary: Clause 60 makes non-compliance with the Minister's orders an offence punishable by a fine up to $100,000 or five years' jail or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 60 makes non-compliance with the Minister’s orders an offence, punishable by a fine of up to $100,000 or five years’ jail or both.

sections.label: Unauthorised photography of Protected Areas
sections.summary: Clause 29 makes unauthorised photography of the whole or any part of a Protected Area or Protected Place an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To address this, clause 29 will make unauthorised photography of the whole or any part of a Protected Area or Protected Place an offence.

sections.label: Photography by unmanned aerial vehicles
sections.summary: Clause 30 deals specifically with photography by unmanned aerial vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 30 deals specifically with photography by unmanned aerial vehicles.

sections.label: Officers' powers over security threats
sections.summary: Clauses 27 and 28 provide authorised officers with powers to identify and deal with potential security threats in the surrounding area.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clauses 27 and 28 provide authorised officers with powers to identify and deal with potential security threats in the surrounding area.

sections.label: Specialist Professional Engineers Protective Security
sections.summary: MHA and the Professional Engineers Board will create a new specialist Professional Engineers category in Protective Security to recognise and develop local expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MHA and the Professional Engineers Board will establish a new category of specialist Professional Engineers in Protective Security   scheme to recognise and develop local expertise.

sections.label: Infrastructure Protection Bill regulatory framework
sections.summary: The Government sees a need for a regulatory framework, and the Infrastructure Protection Bill will require key buildings to incorporate security into their design.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have thus far relied on engagement and persuasion rather than the law.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: But given the heightened threat environment, the Government is of the view that there is a need to establish a regulatory framework to more systematically protect Singapore’s infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With the Infrastructure Protection Bill, key buildings will be required to incorporate security into their design.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These include critical infrastructure delivering essential services, as well as large or iconic buildings that face a higher threat due to high public footfall, or their prominence or symbolic significance.

sections.label: Highest terrorism threat level
sections.summary: The Singapore Terrorism Threat Assessment Report says the threat level is the highest in recent years, and the Bill lets the Government require security features in selected buildings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Terrorism Threat Assessment Report, we are facing the highest level of threat in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, the Government will be able to require selected new and existing buildings to put in place features to strengthen their security.

sections.label: Engagement before legislation enforcement
sections.summary: MHA assured it will rely on engagement with facility owners or occupiers before legislation, but information on Government funding and resource support is lacking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MHA has given the assurance that it will continue to rely on engagement with such facilities' owners or occupiers before turning to legislation for enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, while the penalties for non-compliance have been listed clearly in the Bill, information about Government funding and resource support for identified facilities is lacking.

sections.label: Hospitals as protected areas
sections.summary: The speaker requests that hospitals be considered for the list of selected protected areas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last, I would like to request that hospitals be considered for the list of selected protected areas.

sections.label: Fines and photographing protected areas
sections.summary: Maximum fines rose from $1,000 to $20,000, and clause 29 makes photographing or videoing protected areas and places an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the same time, the maximum fines for offences have been drastically increased, from $1,000 to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, clause 29 introduces a new provision to make it an offence to take photographs or videos of protected areas and protected places.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is it reasonable to punish someone taking a picture from outside, when he is standing in a public area, and the photograph is simply capturing what is already visible publicly?

sections.label: Wasted costs under clause 80
sections.summary: Clause 80 requires the owner to bear wasted costs, such as undoing systems or structures already put in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What if the new measures result in wasted costs, for example, if they require undoing of systems or structures already put in?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It seems that, according to clause 80, the owner has to bear such wasted costs.

sections.label: Terrorism Threat Assessment Report release
sections.summary: MHA released a Terrorism Threat Assessment Report on 1 June 2017 and an ISIS video featured a Singapore-born terrorist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On 1 June 2017, MHA released the Terrorism Threat Assessment Report that highlighted the persistent risk of attack that Singapore faces, and the recent video released by the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) media centre featuring a Singapore-born terrorist further brings home the point that security is our collective responsibility.

sections.label: Minister appoints infrastructure protection officers
sections.summary: The Bill vests the Minister with authority to appoint a Commissioner of Infrastructure Protection and Deputy and Assistant Commissioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill, when passed, will vest the Minister with the authority to appoint, among public officers, a Commissioner of Infrastructure Protection, and a team of Deputy Commissioners and Assistant Commissioners that administer the Act.

sections.label: Study on existing buildings security
sections.summary: An interagency working team was formed in April 2016 to study security guidelines for existing buildings, and the study's results will be made available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While these features can be incorporated with relative ease into new developments, they are much more difficult to be implemented in existing buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was reported in April 2016 that an interagency working team has been put together to study security guidelines for existing buildings and the results of the study will be made available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry shed some light on the outcome of this study?

sections.label: Terrorism threat and Bill timeliness
sections.summary: The passage states the terrorism threat is real and persistent and that reading the Bill is timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The threat of terrorism is real and persistent, Mr Speaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Recent sectarian violence in Southeast Asia is not only the result of violent extremism and fundamentalism originating from the Middle East, it also provides the recruitment platform for the extremism and fundamentalism to be fuelled further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is a vicious cycle that will have potentially grave consequences as returning fighters from the conflict in that part of the world come back to this part of the world in Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The reading of this Bill is thus timely and we certainly need to strengthen our resolve to combat extremism and terrorism, not only in terms of being more vigilant, reinforcing our social ties, boosting our paramilitary competencies, but also in protecting our buildings and infrastructure as well.

sections.label: Infrastructure owners adopt security measures
sections.summary: The Bill requires infrastructure owners to adopt measures against security threats, as security agencies cannot be the only active agents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The broad-ranging terrorist arsenal meant that our security agencies cannot be the only active agents in preventing terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to ensure that our key infrastructures are well guarded against threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Infrastructure owners will be required to adopt measures against security threats.

sections.label: Infrastructure selection and compliance timeline
sections.summary: The passage asks how infrastructure is selected, how many buildings are affected, and the compliance timeline for the Bill's requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share more on how the selection of infrastructure is made, and how many buildings will be affected?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: What is the timeline given for affected buildings to comply with all the requirements set out in the Bill?

sections.label: Guidelines for authorised officer powers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the powers given to the authorised officer in clause 22 are subject to guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The presence of the global threat of terror is very real, and the need to empower our officers is much needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, can the Minister clarify if these powers given to the authorised officer in clause 22 are subject to guidelines?

sections.label: Security officer powers and training
sections.summary: The passage asks for clarification on the need for security officer powers and whether MHA will develop the industry and improve training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide further clarifications on the need to provide security officers with such powers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MHA be devoting resources into developing this industry and reviewing and improving the training provided to these officers?

sections.label: Grants for building owners' costs
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to address public concerns about grants for building owners unable to afford implementing directives or orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But perhaps the cost of not implementing such measures against terrorist attacks would be greater than the cost of installing CCTVs, deploying security officers and barriers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But I hope the Minister can address some of the public concerns with regard to the availability of grants in exceptional cases where the building owner is unable to afford the costs of implementing the directives or orders.

sections.label: Private security officers as common group
sections.summary: The passage states that the 42,000 private security officers on the ground today are treated as a common group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For private security officers today, the 42,000 of them on the ground are treated as a common group.

sections.label: Officers near or post-retirement
sections.summary: The passage states that about one-third of the 42,000 officers today are near retirement or post-retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On the other hand, based on our ground engagement, about one-third of the 42,000 officers today are near retirement or post-retirement.

sections.label: Security industry employment issues
sections.summary: The security industry faces long working hours, lack of proper rest areas, and only basic statutory employment benefits for officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Currently, the security industry is plagued by issues, such as long working hours, lack of proper rest areas, and officers are given only basic employment statutory benefits.

sections.label: Reduced demand for security officers
sections.summary: These could reduce overall demand for private security officers, allowing shorter working hours than the current 12 hours a day, six days a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: All these could reduce the overall demand for private security officers to allow for shorter working hours which are currently at 12 hours a day for six days a week.

sections.label: Demand increase under new law
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry foresees a sizeable increase in demand for security officers under the new law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the new law, does the Ministry foresee a sizeable increase in demand for security officers?

sections.label: Costs, co-funding and upskilling
sections.summary: Costs passed to tenants and consumers prompt a request for co-funding for older buildings and higher funding for advanced technologies, requiring officers to upskill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These costs will be passed down to the tenants, many of whom are small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and eventually trickle down to consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like the Ministry to consider extending co-funding support to older buildings seeking to comply with the Bill and incentivise building owners to adopt more advanced technologies by providing higher funding support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The introduction of advanced technologies will also mean that existing security officers must upgrade and upskill themselves to remain relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand that such concerns have already been raised to the Security Industry Transformation Committee, and an Industry Transformation Map (ITM) for the Private Security Industry is due by the end of this year.

sections.label: Batam rocket attack attempt
sections.summary: The recent attempt by terrorists to fire a rocket from Batam shows terrorists exploring all means to cause casualties and instill fear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The recent attempt by terrorists to fire a rocket from Batam is a clear example of terrorists exploring all means to cause casualties and instill fear.

sections.label: Security-by-design construction cost
sections.summary: In past projects where security-by-design was implemented, security measures cost between 0.2% and 3% of total construction cost.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In past projects where security-by-design was implemented, the cost of security measures was between 0.2% and 3% of the total construction cost.

sections.label: Special Infrastructure designation criteria
sections.summary: Developments over 100,000 square metres in specific planning areas, designated by URA for commercial, community and mixed use, will be included, and existing buildings meeting criteria generally designated as Special Infrastructures.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For a start, we will include developments with a gross floor area of over 100,000 square metres, are located in specific planning areas, and there is a list which will be identified in the Gazette.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And apart from the gross floor area of 100,000 square metres, and also the location being in specific planning areas, these buildings ought to be designated by URA for commercial, community and mixed use.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Existing buildings that meet the criteria will generally also be designated as Special Infrastructures so that security can be incorporated in their design during renovation.

sections.label: Commissioner assesses each project
sections.summary: The Commissioner will assess each project after assessing the person's relevant qualifications, past security-by-design experience, and the project's nature.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Commissioner will make an assessment for each project, after assessing the person’s relevant qualifications, past experience with security-by-design projects, and the nature of the project.

sections.label: Counterterrorism course licensing requirement
sections.summary: MHA and SPF are working with Security Tripartite Cluster stakeholders to make the counterterrorism course a licensing requirement for more security officers and incorporate it in the Progressive Wage Model.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MHA and SPF are working with stakeholders in the Security Tripartite Cluster to make this counterterrorism course a licensing requirement for more security officers and incorporate this in the Progressive Wage Model.

sections.label: Residential buildings security risk assessments
sections.summary: Mr Zainal Sapari suggested mandating security risk assessments for all residential buildings, but the general threat assessment does not yet warrant a blanket requirement on the thousands of such buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Zainal Sapari suggested mandating that all residential buildings carry out security risk assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are thousands of such buildings and the general threat assessment does not yet warrant a blanket requirement on all of them.

sections.label: Interagency review of guidelines update
sections.summary: Mr Darryl David asked for an update on the interagency review of the guidelines, which is ongoing and hoped to be published by early 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Darryl David asked for an update on the interagency review of the guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is ongoing and we hope to publish the revised guidelines by early 2018.

sections.label: Unauthorised photography offence penalties
sections.summary: The Bill will make unauthorised photography an offence punishable with a fine of up to $20,000 or imprisonment of up to two years or both, with signs displayed at the perimeter of the Protected Area or Place.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Bill will make unauthorised photography an offence punishable with a fine of up to $20,000 or imprisonment of up to two years or both, and signs will be displayed at the perimeter of the Protected Area or Place.

sections.label: Fine increase for Protected Areas
sections.summary: The Bill raises the fine for offences relating to Protected Areas and Places from $1,000 to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The existing offence provisioned under section (7) of the Act is a fine of $1,000 and two years' imprisonment or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, under the Bill, the fine for offences relating to Protected Areas and Places is increased to $20,000.

sections.label: Infrastructure Protection Bill and Sitting
sections.summary: The Infrastructure Protection Bill is described as a step against terrorist attacks, and the Sitting is suspended until 4.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Infrastructure Protection Bill is an important step forward as we fortify Singapore's resolve against the threat of terrorist attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: You will be glad to know that we will have 20 minutes this time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.30 pm.
